title: An executor rewriting its own task's acceptance criteria retires a failed evaluation
outcome: An implementer cannot clear a failing acceptance evaluation by rewriting the criteria it failed; criteria changes by the run's holder or executors are either refused, or keep the failure in force until someone else accepts the revision.
acceptance: A test shows that an executor's criteria revision cannot turn a fresh failing evaluation into a completable task without the decided safeguard
Revisions by someone other than the executor, and revisions made with no failing evaluation, behave as today
The acceptance-evaluation design doc states the rule
The rule for acceptance revisions made by the run's holder or an executor after a fresh failing evaluation is decided with Greg and recorded

completion.summary:
A failing acceptance evaluation now survives an executor's rewrite of the criteria it judged, until someone other than the executor accepts the revision.

43c94d6 carried the failure: after a revision of the criteria or bindings it judged, it is shown, and it must be named with --supersedes after the executor's revision. e450eb0 implements Greg's decision "so B it is": the naming evaluation must come from an evaluator that never held the run (carried_failure_self_acknowledged otherwise). A failing evaluation that names the failure keeps it carried; only a passing one ends it, or the run ending (K3). show --full gives the evaluator the original, newest and current contracts.

The acceptance-evaluation design doc records it as R11, with rows B53–B58. Both landings were reviewed to a clean round and gated on the committed tree; build 4eb402bb7df2 is installed.
